label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. The harness withheld recent_deploys, service_health: each call to it got the error its source gives when it does not answer, and never reached that source (an outage simulated for this case; the stack itself was not touched). Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 13 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: evt_000272 (payment.succeeded, pay_000247, $104.44) was delivered twice, 0.5 s apart, which is normal at-least-once delivery. webhook-receiver queued both copies to provider-events/1, at offsets 123 and 124. At ＠123 ledger-consumer ran INSERT INTO processed_events ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and then posted. At ＠124 it went straight to INSERT transactions and entries, with no processed_events insert or check, and posted again. This created ledger transactions 272 and 275. The duplicate is balanced, so ledger_balanced passes, but it fails posted_exactly_once and puts provider_clearing $104.44 ahead of the provider (matches_provider). payment-confirmer was idempotent both times, so only the ledger is wrong. Why dedup was skipped on ＠124 is not shown. It may be a recent change to the ledger-consumer handler or settings, or a code path that bypasses processed_events. Deploy history could not be read (c4).

evidence.shows: The money check settled and still failed. evt_000272 was posted 2 times, as transactions 272 and 275. The ledger is +10444 cents against the provider, all of it on pay_000247 (ledger 20888 vs provider 10444). The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds all match the provider.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000272 twice (key pay_000247): partition 1 offset 123 at 22:17:49.920 and offset 124 at 22:17:50.420. The two copies have different trace ids.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000272 twice: source provider-events/1＠123 at 22:17:49.923 and ＠124 at 22:17:50.668.

First delivery (offset 123): the ledger span runs INSERT INTO processed_events ... ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING, then INSERT transactions and INSERT entries, with outcome posted. The confirmer reports already_confirmed.

Second delivery (offset 124): the ledger span starts at about 248 ms. It runs only an empty-text db span, INSERT transactions and INSERT entries, with no processed_events statement, and outcome posted. The confirmer again reports already_confirmed. The receiver answered 200 to both copies.
The ledger counted 21.25 already_processed in the last 10 min, so its dedup path does work for some messages. The skip is not total.
ledger-consumer logged no warnings or errors in the last hour, so no error explains the skipped dedup.
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer. Whether ledger-consumer was recently redeployed or reconfigured is unknown.

proposed_fix.summary: First, a human should confirm in the deploy log that ledger-consumer was deployed or reconfigured shortly before 22:17. If so, roll it back to its previous settings to restore dedup on every message. The rollback_deploy action is refused if there is no such deploy. If there was no deploy, fix the handler instead, so that every message does the processed_events insert and checks its result in the same transaction as the posting. Either way, stopping new damage repairs nothing. Duplicate transaction 275 (evt_000272 at offset 124) must still be reversed with a compensating entry, or removed under review. Then rerun the money check and scan the ledger for other events posted more than once.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating the ledger-consumer container pauses ledger posting while it restarts. Kafka keeps the committed offsets, so events wait and are booked after the restart. If the rollback goes to a version with other defects, or the skip has another cause, double-posting continues. The compensating entry for transaction 275 changes ledger balances and must target exactly that transaction. Payments, refunds and payment-confirmer are untouched. All data is synthetic.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the settings it ran before the rollback, as the deploy log records them. Then rerun the money check. If a compensating entry for transaction 275 turns out to be wrong, reverse it with an opposite entry, and do not delete rows.
